Topic: Impact of COVID-19 on Patient Access to Services

Clues (max 200 words): "the only changes that I would say happened in the facility probably is the patients you know because of the fear of COVID 19 many patients are not coming to the hospital." "many of them treat themselves at home but in terms of the health facility they do all what it takes for them to try and see that patients are well treated and well taken care of." "most of them were having this fairness in them that if I come to the hospital that where I will catch COVID." "the sensitization was there, the doctors are seeing their patients and nurses are seeing patients but it just this fear people has in themselves."

Reasoning (max 150 words): The clues illustrate a significant decline in patient access to services due to the fear of contracting COVID-19. The quote regarding patients not coming to the hospital indicates a direct impact on service delivery, while the mention of individuals treating themselves at home shows a shift away from seeking professional medical assistance. The emotional tone of "fairness" highlights the psychological barriers that patients faced, exacerbating the issue. The last clue underscores that despite the healthcare facility's efforts to provide care, the pervasive fear among patients hindered their willingness to seek services, ultimately affecting health outcomes.

Topic: Changes in Health Facility Operations Due to COVID-19

"there are outreaches, people are going out to sensitize people, people are coming in and the sensitization is too much." "the only thing is that everybody was taking that precautions." "we give thanks to God at least there was an early intervention and they were able to combat the situation."

Reasoning (max 150 words): These clues highlight the operational changes within the health facility in response to COVID-19. The first clue emphasizes a collaborative approach taken by all staff members, regardless of their usual roles, to manage the outbreak. The reference to outreach and sensitization efforts indicates proactive measures taken to educate the public about COVID-19, showcasing adaptations in communication strategies. The mention of precautions reflects a shift in operational protocols aimed at minimizing risk. Lastly, the acknowledgment of early intervention underscores the facility's capacity to respond effectively to the crisis, indicating a commitment to maintaining service delivery despite challenges.

Topic: Financial Challenges and Revenue Generation During COVID-19

Clues (max 200 words): "the hospital was generating revenue but because of this COVID now people were not coming so everything was just on standstill in terms of generating revenue." "yes the revenue fall because patients were not coming because they fear that if they come to the hospital they will catch COVID 19." "government will send subvention that we use mainly to run the hospital because the revenue is so small."

Reasoning (max 150 words): The clues highlight the financial challenges faced by the healthcare facility during the COVID-19 pandemic. The respondent notes a significant decline in revenue generation due to decreased patient visits, directly linked to fears of contracting the virus. This reduction in revenue created financial strain, necessitating reliance on government subventions to maintain operations. The clues underscore how external factors like public fear and health crises can disrupt the financial sustainability of healthcare institutions, indicating the need for adaptive financial strategies in times of crisis.

Topic: Experience and Preparedness from the Ebola Outbreak

Clues (max 200 words): "during the EBOLA I was in Sierra Leone," "the experience that we had during the EBOLA that what helped us during this corona," "the way people died during the EBOLA cannot be compared to the COVID," "this time round we had more awareness and sensitization."

Reasoning (max 150 words): These clues illustrate the influence of the Ebola outbreak on the response to COVID-19. The respondent’s acknowledgment of being in Sierra Leone during Ebola suggests firsthand experience, which lends credibility to the comparison. The statement "the experience that we had during the EBOLA that what helped us during this corona" indicates that lessons learned from Ebola informed the strategies implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic. Additionally, the reflection that "the way people died during the EBOLA cannot be compared to the COVID" suggests a perception of improved outcomes during COVID-19, possibly due to enhanced preparedness and awareness. The emphasis on "more awareness and sensitization" signals a shift towards proactive public health communication, illustrating how past experiences shaped current responses.
